newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Battle for Swedish mortgage bank hots up.
newsitem.headline: Battle for Swedish mortgage bank hots up.

text.p: Swedish high street bank Handelsbanken looked set on Thursday to bid for mortgage bank Stadshypotek, challenging Swedish insurer Skandia's proposed merger offer.
Handelsbanken said it would hold a news conference in Stockholm at 1500 GMT concerning Stadshypotek which is Sweden's largest mortgage lender with one third of the market.

Brokers said it appeared certain the bank would reveal a competing bid to rival the proposed merger announced by Skandia on November 25 that valued Stadshypotek at around 20.6 billion crowns ($3.02 billion).

"Handelsbanken's press conference announcement should not only mean that it will place a bid on Stadshypotek but also that (insurer) Skandia did not want to or could not match that bid," one broker said.
The government, which is seeking to sell the state's 34 percent holding in Stadshypotek, has voiced fierce opposition to the Skandia/Stadshypotek merger proposal.
Finance Minister Erik Asbrik has said no decision would be announced on the sale of the state's stake until an auction process, that was opened on December 2, was completed.
The Swedish Finance Minister on Thursday said it would make an announcement regarding Stadshypotek at 1530 GMT.
Svenska Handelsbanken is Sweden's largest bank in the country by asset size with a significant market share in both corporate and retail banking.
Handelsbanken had been tipped by some market players as the best suitor for Stadshypotek in economic terms and as best placed to take on major mortgage interests.
U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's last week upgraded Handelbanken's outlook to positive from stable.
Handelsbanken for the first nine months of 1996 posted a 19 percent increase in profit after credit losses of 4.52 billion crowns ($663 million).
